title: Brokered slot allocator for embeddings with tenant smoothing and proportional rate fencing
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: Embedding endpoints see large, short-lived surges from a small number of tenants (hotkeys) that cause head-of-line blocking, degraded p99 latency, and noisy autoscale churn. Current per-tenant hard rate limits and global autoscaler react too slowly for bursty loads, causing latency SLO violations and overprovisioning.

Goal: Build a brokered slot allocator and tenant smoothing layer that: 1) dynamically assigns short-lived execution slots to tenants based on forecasted headroom and proportional fairness, 2) applies soft and hard rate fencing to bound tail latency without catastrophic drops, 3) integrates with our autoscaler to avoid unnecessary scale-ups on short bursts, and 4) surfaces metrics for capacity planning. This ticket is the engineering implementation and rollout for the allocator and smoothing policy for the embeddings service (runtimes handling text-embedding models).
acceptance_criteria: 1) P99 latency for embeddings under synthetic burst tests (tenant skew 90:5:5) improves by >=35% compared to baseline for the same cost budget
2) Autoscaler scale-up events classified as "burst" are reduced by >=40% in the staged cluster
3) No customer-visible 5xx regression during canary (<=0.02% of requests),
4) Per-tenant fairness metric (90th percentile rate share relative to committed weight) within 15% of target for top 100 tenants
implementation_notes: Architecture: Introduce a lightweight broker service colocated with ingress that maintains a small pool of time-sliced slots per GPU pool. Slots = execution permits allowing request admission into runtime queues.
Allocation algorithm: hybrid of token-bucket smoothing + proportional-share allocator. Short-lived forecasting (5s horizon) informs transient headroom reservations for known hotkeys.
Backpressure behavior: implement two-tier gating: soft (latency-preserving delaying via token wait) and hard (reject with 429 + retry-after) with tenant-configurable priorities.

Autoscaler integration: broker exposes observed short-burst load and sustained load signals. Autoscaler will ignore bursts under configured threshold to avoid scale churn. Add a suppression window of 60s for burst-driven scale-ups.
Data-plane hooks: modify embedding router to request slots from broker before enqueue. Keep fallback path: if broker unresponsive, fallback to existing admission (fail-open for <=1% requests).
Performance: keep broker critical path <600us median and <3ms p99 on tx path. Use eBPF-ish socket pooling and in-process caches where possible.
Config: tenant weight, soft/hard quotas, suppression windows, forecast horizon are dynamic flags exposed in Console and via feature gates for gradual rollout.
rollout_plan: 1) Unit + integration tests in CI; benchmark harness added to embeddings perf suite
2) Deploy broker to staging embedding pool; run synthetic burst campaign (replay from production traces) for 48h
3) Canary on 5% traffic in us-west-2 with conservative defaults (aggressive suppression, larger delays), monitor p99/p50, error rates
4) Expand to 20% with customer opt-in and targeted tenants (low-risk), keep suppression window at 60s
5) Measure cost metrics and adjust autoscaler thresholds; full scale rollout to remaining pools after 2 weeks of stable canary metrics
6) Postmortem/learnings and doc updates in Confluence after full rollout
comments: 2026-01-26 - Asha Patel: Kickoff meeting notes: agreed to keep broker stateless where possible; persistence only for short horizon telemetry. Action: Marco to prototype token allocator by EOW.

2026-02-02 - Marco Ruiz: Prototype ready (local): token-bucket + proportional allocator; local benchmarks show 2.1x reduction in p99 under synthetic 10x burst. Observed slot_acquire_latency p99=2.8ms. Shared prototype in GitHub: https://github.com/redwood-inference/emb-runtime/pull/4826

2026-02-15 - Design review (eng+infra): Feedback to add fail-open fallback and metrics for suppressed scaleups. Agree to suppression window default=60s and make configurable. Action: add canary dashboards.

2026-02-25 - QA: Integration tests added to perf harness (replay of 2026-01-14 incident trace). Test shows autoscaler suppression prevented a scale-up but increased request queuing; we tuned soft-quota to reduce added latency.
2026-03-03 - Security review: No secrets in broker; uses existing mTLS between services. Recommend audit log entry for quota rejections (added).

2026-03-08 - Marco Ruiz: Canary started in us-west-2 (5% traffic). Early signal: p99 improved ~28% and 429s at 0.01% for top tenants. Observed broker p99 slot_acquire_latency=3.4ms; investigating tail latencies.
2026-03-10 - Asha Patel: Updated acceptance criteria added to align with cost budget requirements and fairness metric. Next: tuning weights and running economy tests.
